limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_in_progress.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount of the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount of the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (bitwise AND of the two amounts is zero)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.meaning: the limit order match is rejected as a zero-cost trade

assumptions: The zero-cost validation check is the only rejection mechanism considered for this claim.
Matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities at the validation checkpoint.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the disjoint-bits precondition is encoded as a grounded Boolean rather than a bitwise relation.

limitations: The disjoint-bits condition is represented by a Boolean because the plan grammar has no bitwise-AND predicate; the report's numeric examples (256 & 255 = 0, 40 & 21) are not encoded as arithmetic.
The impact text describes scope over all limit order matching rather than a distinct post-state; the impact outcome is encoded as the rejection event itself.

links.reported_relation: The bitwise AND instead of logical OR causes false positives when legitimate trade amounts have no overlapping bits, rejecting legitimate matches as zero-cost trades.
The faulty condition affects all limit order matching, both partial and full matches.
